locale.name: English
dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Runs stream here as they happen. Everything below is the ledger they produced.
dashboard.descriptionIdle: Receipts pulled from email, parsed and checked.
dashboard.runFinishedSub: Each email shows every step the graph took to reach its numbers.
dashboard.connectBody: Signing in with Google grants read-only Gmail access. Receipts are parsed on your server, the refresh token is encrypted at rest, and nothing is written back to your mailbox.
transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.description: Every receipt in the ledger. Open a row to see which step decided each field, and whether it came from a pattern, the model, or you.
transactions.pinned: Showing the {count} receipts behind an insight.
transactions.pinnedOne: Showing the 1 receipt behind an insight.
review.title: Review
review.description: Receipts the graph could not close out — a missing vendor, a total that does not reconcile. It paused mid-run rather than guess. Answering one resumes it from where it stopped.
review.expiredNote: This checkpoint has expired, so the sender and subject are no longer in memory. The numbers below are what was kept.
review.resumeNote: Your values re-enter the graph at await_review and pass back through validate before anything is written — the same arithmetic the model had to satisfy. A vendor you set is remembered for this sender.
insights.title: Insights
insights.description: Patterns that only show up across months — what you are committed to each year, which subscriptions went up, duplicate charges, and where your spend concentrates.
insights.nothingAnomalousSub: No duplicate charges, price jumps, or outliers in the current ledger.
finding.duplicate.title: Possible duplicate charge at {vendor}
finding.duplicate.detail: {amount} charged twice within {days} day(s) — check for a double billing or two confirmation emails for one order.
finding.outlier.title: Unusually large charge at {vendor}
finding.missing_tax.title: No tax recorded for {vendor}
finding.missing_tax.detail: {vendor} charged tax on {with_tax} of {receipts} receipts, but this {amount} charge has none.
finding.price_increase.title: {vendor} went up {pct}%
finding.lapsed.title: No charge from {vendor} since {last_charged}
finding.lapsed.detail: A {cadence} charge is {days_overdue} days late — either it was cancelled, or the receipt never arrived.
finding.needs_review.title: {count} receipt(s) still need a human
finding.needs_review.detail: These are excluded from nothing — they are in your totals with the values the pipeline could prove, which may be incomplete.
trace.resolve.unresolved: vendor not resolved by the rules
trace.persist.discarded: recorded as discarded so it is not parsed again
issue.amount_not_positive: The amount is zero or negative
issue.tax_exceeds_plausible_share: Tax is too large a share of the total
issue.total_does_not_reconcile: Subtotal plus tax does not equal the total
issue.date_in_future: The date is in the future
issue.date_unparseable: The date could not be read
settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Connections, and what happens to your data.
settings.gmailNotConnected: Not connected — read-only access, revocable from your Google account
settings.assistedOn: On — a model fills only the fields the rules cannot prove
settings.assistedOff: Off — vendors still resolve, but awkward totals will need reviewing
settings.languageSub: Applies to everything on the page, including parse traces.
settings.data1: Gmail access is read-only. Nothing is sent, labelled, or deleted in your mailbox.
settings.data2: The refresh token is encrypted with your server's Fernet key before it is written to disk, and removing it here deletes it.
settings.data3: Email bodies are not stored. Only the extracted fields, the parse trace, and the Gmail message id are kept — the id is what stops the next sync re-parsing the same receipt.
settings.data4: When a field needs the model, only the financially relevant lines are sent, not the whole email.
reason.marketing: marketing copy with no purchase evidence
reason.amount_only: an amount, but no purchase wording
reason.model_unavailable: model unavailable, used the amount heuristic
statement.title: Statement
notifications.title: Notifications
statement.description: Recomputed from the ledger every time you open this, so nothing here can be out of date.
notifications.description: Everything the last runs turned up.
statement.headerDescription: One month closed out: what changed against last month, sales tax paid, and the three exports — a plain ledger, an accounting journal, and an expense claim.
issue.model_unavailable: The model could not be reached, so the gap was never filled
review.blockedNote: Nothing is wrong with this receipt. The model was unavailable when it ran, so the missing field was never filled — re-syncing once it is reachable will usually clear this without you doing anything.
review.splitBoth: {blocked} waiting on the model · {human} waiting on you
notifications.headerDescription: Everything the last runs turned up, newest first. Opening one takes you to the receipts behind it.
advisor.title: Advisor
advisor.description: Questions about your own spending, answered from the ledger. It sees your totals by month, category and merchant — never a receipt, never an email.
advisor.disclaimer: Not a licensed financial advisor. This is general information drawn from your receipts, not personal financial, tax or legal advice — for anything that turns on your full circumstances, ask a qualified professional.
advisor.emptyBody: It can only see aggregates — what you spent by month, by category and by merchant. Try one of these:
advisor.s1: Where is most of my money going?
advisor.s2: Which subscriptions should I look at?
advisor.s3: How does this month compare to my average?
advisor.signedOut: Sign in or run the sample inbox first — there is nothing to advise on yet.
advisor.failed: The advisor could not be reached.
home.tagline: Receipts in your inbox become a ledger you can check.
home.lede: Every figure carries the steps that produced it — which pattern matched, where a merchant came from, what the model was asked and what it answered. When the arithmetic does not hold, the run stops and asks you rather than guessing.
home.tryIt: Try it with a sample inbox
home.tryItSub: Ninety-odd generated receipts, run through the real pipeline. No account, no Gmail access.
home.orConnectSub: Read-only, revocable, and no email body is ever stored.
home.graphSub: Eight nodes and two loops. Rules answer what they can prove; the model is only asked about the gaps; a person is only asked when neither could settle it.
nav.demoNote: Demo data, not an account. Signing in replaces it.
home.step1Body: Rules pull what they can prove — the total, the tax, the merchant from the sending domain. Most receipts never need anything else.
home.step2Body: Only the fields the rules could not settle, and only the financially relevant lines are sent — never the whole email.
home.step3Body: Subtotal plus tax has to equal the total, and every field has to be worth trusting — a value read off a clean pattern counts for more than one a model inferred. Fail either test and the run stops and asks you, rather than banking a number it cannot stand behind.
